portfolio.note: Total PEP payoff across the portfolio is $1.4 million as of 9/2, down from a little over $2 million at the start, through buybacks and not adding new loans. Seven Winterwood homes carry roughly $350,000 of that, with three close to $60,000 each.

notes.text: GRP needs $24,447 to reach zero. True bank is negative $16,575, so the account is overdrawn rather than short on paper. Four entities could cover it alone: Countryside $33,162 above a $5,000 floor, Four Seasons $30,746, Winterwood $18,731 and Decade Acres $11,265. Four Seasons has never funded a GRP transfer; Countryside has carried every one.

The forecast does not go short but the last week of October falls to $3,735. WW:6D at $36,500 in the week of 9/25 is what keeps the window positive. October has five Thursdays, so the fourth week weighting is split across 10/23 and 10/30. Opening cash is the true bank balance of $130,280.

cfo_summary: Total available cash is $125,049 against a true bank balance of $130,280. After $8,292 in external payments and no intercompany transfers, projected end of week is $116,757. Ten bills, the lightest run since 8/28.

GRP is overdrawn at the bank at negative $16,575 and projects to negative $24,447 after this week's $4,672. It received $29,747 in management fees on 9/4 and still fell $9,924 in seven days. Against $15,600 of bills on that run, roughly $24,000 cleared outside the payables template. This is the fifth negative week in twelve and the third consecutive week that GRP movement has not been traceable to the bill run.

A transfer is required this week and there are no management fees to fix it. Holding every other entity at a $5,000 floor, capacity is Countryside $33,162, Four Seasons $30,746, Winterwood $18,731, Decade Acres $11,265 and Country Aire $10,493. Four Seasons has $35,746, no bills this week, and has not funded a GRP transfer in sixteen weeks. Countryside has carried every one, including $68,615 on 8/21.

The rest of the portfolio is the strongest it has been. Available cash rose $43,227 in a week. Seven entities improved, four hold more than $15,000, and only Riverside at $5,513 and Group Group at $85 sit below $6,000. Group Group has been at $85 for four straight weeks; distributions to it usually run week three.

The forecast stays positive but ends thin. The last week of October falls to $3,735. WW:6D at $36,500 in the week of 9/25 is what holds the window up, and it was expected to close this week. Confirm timing with Justin before sizing the transfer, because if 6D lands in GRP it covers most of the hole on its own.

Committed watchlist activity sits in the next two weeks. $2,000 in and $10,610 out the week of 9/18 for the FS1:23 demo and Rico's 44 Waterway labor, then $36,500 in against the $7,000 Vincent lien the week of 9/25.

PEP floor plan is two homes at $60,745. 2125 Patricia at $29,903 due November 29, and DA: 54 at $30,842 which will be bought back with no date set. RE: 11 and CP: 77 JPL are delinquent but monitoring only.

for_ownership.label: Projected end-of-week cash
for_ownership.paragraph: We close this week at roughly $116,800 available across all accounts after a light bill run of $8,300. The portfolio is in the strongest position it has been in months, with four accounts holding more than $15,000. The exception is Golden Rule Practices, which is overdrawn at the bank by about $16,600 and needs a transfer of roughly $24,400 this week. It received $30,000 in management fees last week and still went further negative, and about $24,000 of that movement is not traceable to the bill run. Winterwood 6D is under contract at $36,500 and was expected to close this week; those proceeds would cover most of the shortfall. Looking out sixty days the business stays positive but ends October thin.
